h3. Description / User Impact

When creating an OSD GCP cluster with Shared VPC + WIF, the DNS Zone dropdown in the VPC Settings step shows all GCP DNS zones matching the domain prefix and organization — including zones already associated with another cluster. If a user selects an already-used zone, the cluster creation request will fail with a backend validation error. The dropdown should only show unused (unassigned) DNS zones to prevent this.

h3. Environment

Environment: All (Production, Staging)
URL: {{/openshift/create/osd > Networking > VPC Settings}}
Browser: Any
OS: Any

h3. Steps to Reproduce

# Create a GCP DNS zone via CLI and associate it with an existing cluster
# Begin creating a new OSD GCP cluster with Shared VPC + WIF and the same domain prefix
# Navigate to Networking > VPC Settings
# Observe the DNS Zone dropdown

h3. Expected Result

The DNS Zone dropdown should only show zones not already associated with a cluster. The existing {{getDnsDomains}} service function already supports this via the search parameter {{cluster.id=''}} where {{cluster.id=''}} means "not associated with any cluster" (i.e., unused/available). The GCP-specific {{getGcpDnsDomains}} function should add this same filter.

h3. Actual Result

The DNS Zone dropdown shows all GCP DNS zones for the org/prefix, including zones already in use by other clusters. Selecting an in-use zone will result in a backend error on cluster creation submission.

h3. Root Cause

In {{src/services/clusterService.ts}}, the {{getGcpDnsDomains}} function (line ~413) only filters by {{cloud_provider='gcp'}} and optionally by {{id}}. It does not include {{cluster.id=''}} in the search parameter to exclude zones already associated with a cluster.

The generic {{getDnsDomains}} function (line ~386) already supports this pattern via its {{hasCluster}} parameter, which builds {{cluster.id!=''}} or {{cluster.id=''}} search filters. {{getGcpDnsDomains}} does not use this same pattern.

Additionally, the client-side filter in {{useFetchGcpDnsDomains.ts}} only filters by {{domain_prefix}} and {{organization.id}} — no cluster association check at any layer.

h3. Suggested Fix

Add {{cluster.id=''}} to the search clauses in {{getGcpDnsDomains}} so only unused DNS zones are returned in the wizard dropdown. The corrected search would be:

{code:sql}cloud_provider='gcp' AND cluster.id=''{code}

h3. References

* Original implementation: *OCMUI-4151* (PR #409) by Dylan Cooper
* Related: *OCMUI-4244* (PR #414) — DNS Zone Day 2 display
* Discovered during: *OCMUI-4472* BYO Firewall Rules DDR analysis
* API: {{DnsCloudProvider}} enum supports {{aws | gcp}} — only GCP has a DNS Zone wizard UI

* Implement Playwright end-to-end test coverage for the Networking tab and all supported actions and operations within the tab.
* Ensure the tests validate the Networking tab functionality end-to-end, including relevant user interactions and expected outcomes.
* The coverage should be implemented for ROSA clusters, with ROSA Hosted (HCP) as the preferred target.

h2. Overview

As an OCM cluster administrator with a 4.x cluster, I want to receive proper upgrade notifications and accurate messaging when OCP 5.0 becomes available as an upgrade target, so that I can make informed decisions about upgrading to the next major version.

Currently, when OCP 5.0 appears in a cluster's available upgrades:

* [OSD Only] The "New minor version available" alert on the cluster's Settings tab (left side, update strategy section) *does not appear* — the alert only fires for minor version upgrades (e.g., 4.20 → 4.21), not major (4.22 → 5.0). This alert only applies to OSD clusters (by design — its action toggles a setting not supported on ROSA HCP).

_(screenshot updated to 5.0.0 to illustrate the issue)_
!CleanShot 2026-07-08 at 17.20.13-20260708-212215.png|width=838,alt="CleanShot 2026-07-08 at 17.20.13-20260708-212215.png"!
* The "Y stream update" warning in the Update status panel (right side) fires for any non-patch upgrade on *all cluster types* (including ROSA) — open question whether calling a major version jump (4.22 → 5.0) a "Y stream update" is appropriate (pending UX confirmation from Maggie Chen)

_(screenshot updated to 5.0.0 to illustrate the issue)_
!CleanShot 2026-07-08 at 17.06.05-20260708-211308.png|width=356,alt="CleanShot 2026-07-08 at 17.06.05-20260708-211308.png"!
* Users on automatic update policies may not realize OCP 5.0 is available because the notification that prompts them to allow the next version never fires (OSD only)

*Two separate UI elements are affected:*

||*Element*||*Location*||*Affected cluster types*||*Issue*||
|"New minor version available" alert (blue, expandable)|Left side — update strategy section|OSD only (suppressed on ROSA HCP by design)|Does not detect major version jumps (logic bug)|
|"Y stream update" warning (yellow triangle)|Right side — Update status panel|All cluster types (ROSA, OSD, etc.)|Detection works correctly — only the copy may be wrong for X-stream upgrades|

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* [OSD] When OCP 5.0 is listed in a 4.x cluster's available upgrades, the cluster's Update status panel displays the "New minor version available" notification alerting the user that a new version is available (OSD clusters)
* When a user on any cluster type sees a 5.x version as the next upgrade target, the "Y stream update" warning uses appropriate language (pending UX confirmation on whether "Y stream update" is correct for a major version boundary)
* Existing minor version upgrade notifications continue to work as before (4.20 → 4.21 still shows "Y stream update" and fires the alert correctly)
* A user on a 5.0 cluster with 5.1 available sees the same alert behavior as minor version upgrades on 4.x (normal operation)
* Unit tests cover major version upgrade scenarios (4.x → 5.0)

h2. How To Reproduce

There are two elements to test — one requires OSD, the other works on any cluster type.

h3. "Y stream update" warning (all cluster types, including ROSA)

*Requirements:*

* Any cluster type (ROSA HCP, ROSA Classic, OSD)
* The cluster must be on a version where the upgrade graph offers a path to the *next minor* version
* "Recurring updates" must be selected, with {{enable_minor_version_upgrades}} off (the default)

*Steps:*

# Use or create a cluster on a version with a Y-stream upgrade edge (e.g., 4.20.27 in the fast channel has a path to 4.21.22)
# Switch the channel to one that includes the next minor (e.g., {{fast-4.21}})
# Wait a few minutes for the backend to recalculate {{available_upgrades}}
# Go to *Settings tab* → the *Update status panel* (right side) should show:
#* _"Your update strategy is currently set to recurring updates. Update 4.21.22 is a Y stream update and must be individually updated."_

h3. "New minor version available" alert (OSD only)

*Requirements:*

* An *OSD cluster* (ROSA HCP clusters use STS, which suppresses this alert by design — the alert's action toggles {{enable_minor_version_upgrades}}, a setting not exposed on ROSA HCP)
* Same version/channel requirements as above
* "Recurring updates" must be selected
* No unmet acknowledgement gates

*Steps:*

# Create an OSD GCP WIF cluster on version *4.20.x* (fast channel)
# Wait for the cluster to finish provisioning (~45 min)
# On the Overview tab, switch the channel from {{fast-4.20}} to {{fast-4.21}}
# Wait a few minutes for the backend to recalculate {{available_upgrades}}
# Go to *Settings tab* → ensure "Recurring updates" is selected and saved
# The *left side* (update strategy section) should show the blue expandable alert: "New minor version available" with action link "Allow the next minor version update"

*Why you need 4.20.x (as of July 2026):*
The upgrade graph does not yet have edges from any 4.21.x version to 4.22.x. A 4.20 cluster with the {{fast-4.21}} channel is the easiest path to trigger a Y-stream upgrade.

h2. Implementation Details

h3. Logic fix needed: "New minor version available" alert

{{src/components/clusters/common/Upgrades/MinorVersionUpgradeAlert/MinorVersionUpgradeAlertHelpers.ts}} — the {{isNextMinorVersionAvailableHelper}} function does not detect major version jumps:

{code:java}// Before (bug — misses 4.x → 5.0):
return major === fromMajor && minor > fromMinor;

// After:
return major > fromMajor || (major === fromMajor && minor > fromMinor);{code}

h3. Copy change only (no logic fix): "Y stream update" warning

{{src/components/clusters/common/Upgrades/UpgradeAcknowledge/UpgradeAcknowledgeHelpers.ts}} — the detection logic *already handles* major version jumps correctly:

{code:java}const minorPlusUpgrade = toMajor > fromMajor || toMinor > fromMinor;{code}

No fix needed here. The warning already fires for 4.x → 5.0 upgrades.

{{src/components/clusters/common/Upgrades/UpgradeAcknowledge/UpgradeAcknowledgeWarning/UpgradeAcknowledgeWarning.tsx}} — if UX confirms a copy change is needed: when {{toMajor > fromMajor}}, update the "Y stream update" text to appropriate language (pending Maggie Chen's guidance). If "Y stream" is deemed acceptable for major boundaries, no change needed.

h3. Verification only

* {{src/components/clusters/common/Upgrades/MinorVersionUpgradeAlert/MinorVersionUpgradeAlertSelectors.ts}} — verify the selector passes through correctly for major version scenarios
* {{src/components/clusters/common/Upgrades/MinorVersionUpgradeAlert/MinorVersionUpgradeAlert.tsx}} — note the {{isSTSEnabled}} guard; the blue alert is intentionally suppressed on Rosa clusters (its action toggles a setting not applicable to ROSA HCP). No change needed here.

h2. Additional Resources

* Related: [OCMUI-4510|https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/OCMUI-4510] — Releases page documentation links (same root cause, different user flow)
* Test cluster: {{ocmui-osd-4-20-upgrade-test}} (OSD GCP WIF, version 4.20.27, fast channel)

h2. Overview

As an OCM cluster administrator with a 4.x cluster, I want to receive proper upgrade notifications and accurate messaging when OCP 5.0 becomes available as an upgrade target, so that I can make informed decisions about upgrading to the next major version.

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
*Red Hat's positioning:* OCP 5.0 is intentionally designed as an *in-place upgrade* from 4.22 — functionally equivalent to a Y-stream upgrade, not a platform rewrite (unlike 3.x → 4.x which was a complete migration). The backend upgrade path (OCPSTRAT-2797: "Enable OCP 4.22 → OCP 5.0 updates") was already in "Release Pending" status.

*What that means for the upgrade graph:* The backend will add an edge from 4.22.x → 5.0.0 in {{available_upgrades}}, just like they add 4.20.x → 4.21.x today. It's treated identically to a Y-stream upgrade in the backend graph.

*What's NOT automatic:* The user still has to manually initiate it (same as any Y-stream upgrade). "Recurring updates" only auto-applies patches. The warning says "must be individually updated" — that applies to 4.x → 5.0 too.

*The forced-upgrade policy (from the docs read):* Red Hat _will_ auto-upgrade your control plane if you fall out of support (16 months after your minor version's GA). So theoretically, if 4.22 goes EOL and 5.0 is the next supported version, Red Hat could force-upgrade you. But that's a backend lifecycle enforcement, not something our UI controls.
{panel}

Currently, when OCP 5.0 appears in a cluster's available upgrades:

* [OSD Only] The "New minor version available" alert on the cluster's Settings tab (left side, update strategy section) *does not appear* — the alert only fires for minor version upgrades (e.g., 4.20 → 4.21), not major (4.22 → 5.0). This alert only applies to OSD clusters (by design — its action toggles a setting not supported on ROSA HCP).

h2. Overview

As an OCM developer, I want all version availability gates centralized in one place so that future OCP releases (5.x, 6.x) don't require hunting through scattered files to update version thresholds.

Today, ~11 version availability gates are spread across ~8 different files in the codebase. Each gate checks whether an OCP version meets a minimum to enable a UI feature (IMDS, ingress, PSC, secure boot, etc.). They all work correctly for OCP 5.x (since 5.x > 4.x satisfies all minimums), but the scattered pattern is a maintenance risk: new features will inevitably add new one-off checks in random files.

h2. Current State

Version gates are defined in:

* {{src/components/clusters/wizards/common/constants.ts}} — {{canSelectImds}} (≥ 4.11), {{canConfigureDayOneManagedIngress}} (≥ 4.14), {{canConfigureDayOnePrivateServiceConnect}} (≥ 4.17)
* {{src/components/clusters/ClusterDetailsMultiRegion/components/Networking/NetworkingHelpers.ts}} — {{canConfigureDayTwoManagedIngress}} (≥ 4.13), {{canConfigureLoadBalancer}} (≥ 4.13 for STS)
* {{src/components/clusters/wizards/osd/Networking/VpcSettings/GcpVpcSettings.tsx}} — inline shared VPC ≥ 4.13.15 check
* {{src/components/clusters/wizards/osd/constants.ts}} — {{MIN_SECURE_BOOT_VERSION = '4.13.0'}}
* {{src/components/clusters/wizards/rosa/rosaConstants.ts}} — {{MIN_MANAGED_POLICY_VERSION = '4.11.4'}}
* {{src/components/clusters/ClusterDetailsMultiRegion/.../EditClusterIngressDialog.jsx}} — {{canConfigureAdditionalRouter}} (exact 4.11/4.12 only)
* {{src/common/versionCompatibility.ts}} — security groups (day1: 4.14, day2: 4.11), shared VPC (4.13.9) — *this is the target pattern*

h2. Target State

* All version availability gates consolidated into {{src/common/versionCompatibility.ts}} (which already handles security groups and shared VPC with the correct pattern)
* Each gate uses {{semver.gte}} via the existing {{isCompatibleFeature}} helper
* Consuming components import from one canonical location
* Dead/EOL paths removed (see below)

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* No user-visible behavior changes — all version-gated features (IMDS selection, managed ingress, Private Service Connect, secure boot, shared VPC, managed policy ARNs) continue to appear/hide at the same version thresholds as before
* All version-gated features correctly resolve as available for OCP 5.0+ clusters (no feature is accidentally hidden for 5.x)
* The deprecated "additional router" editing UI (only applicable to EOL 4.11/4.12 clusters) is removed — users on 4.13+ and 5.x are unaffected
* All existing unit and Playwright tests pass without modification (beyond import path changes)
* Version availability gates are consolidated into a single source of truth, making future threshold changes a one-file update

h2. Implementation Details

Extend the existing {{featureCompatibilityMap}} in {{versionCompatibility.ts}} with new entries:

{code:java}[SupportedFeature.IMDS_SELECTION]: { day1: '4.11.0' },
[SupportedFeature.DAY1_MANAGED_INGRESS]: { day1: '4.14.0' },
[SupportedFeature.DAY2_MANAGED_INGRESS]: { day2: '4.13.0' },
[SupportedFeature.PRIVATE_SERVICE_CONNECT]: { day1: '4.17.0' },
[SupportedFeature.SECURE_BOOT]: { day1: '4.13.0' },
[SupportedFeature.MANAGED_POLICY_ARNS]: { day1: '4.11.4' },
[SupportedFeature.GCP_SHARED_VPC]: { day1: '4.13.15', day2: '4.13.15' },{code}

Then replace scattered helpers with calls to {{isCompatibleFeature(SupportedFeature.X, cluster)}}.

For dead code removal: {{canConfigureAdditionalRouter}} gates editing of deprecated additional routers on 4.11/4.12 clusters. Both versions are EOL. Remove the function and associated conditional UI in {{EditClusterIngressDialog.jsx}}.

h2. Long-term Direction

The centralized map is an intermediate step. The ideal end state is for clusters_mgmt to expose per-version capability metadata (e.g., {{version.capabilities: ["imds_v2", "managed_ingress", "private_service_connect"]}}), allowing the frontend to drop hardcoded version thresholds entirely. It consolidates what we have today.

*Relationship to future API-driven work:* This story is not a hard prerequisite for an eventual API migration, but it makes that migration significantly easier. With all version gates centralized in one map ({{featureCompatibilityMap}}), swapping individual entries for API-driven capability checks becomes a single-file change. Without this consolidation, the same API migration would require touching ~8 scattered files across different domains.

h2. Testing

No user-visible changes. Existing unit tests for each feature gate should continue passing. Add a unit test for the centralized map to verify all entries resolve correctly for a sample 5.x version string.

items.fromString:
▎ ⚠ This ticket requires UX and PM refinement before implementation begins.
  ▎ The problem is understood technically, but the right user-facing behavior (what to show, when, and how) needs UX and product input. Do not start implementation until this ticket has been reviewed and acceptance criteria are defined.


  *Background*

[OCMUI-4195|https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/OCMUI-4195] fixed an infinite spinner on the cluster details page for AI (Assisted Installer) clusters when the AI service returns a non-404 error. The fix degrades gracefully by falling back to data from the subscription when the AI
  cluster API call fails.

  However, this silent degradation means the user has no indication that:

* The AI cluster data could not be retrieved
* The displayed information may be incomplete (partial results)

  *Questions for UX / PM refinement*

* Should all three error types (404, 403, 5xx) surface the same message, or should they be differentiated?
* Is a warning alert the right pattern, or something more subtle (e.g. inline empty-state within the AI-specific section only)?
* Should the alert be dismissible, or persistent for the session?
* Is "showing partial results" the right framing, or should the message be more specific about what data is missing?
* Are there edge cases where silently degrading is the right behavior (e.g. 404 for a cluster that was legitimately deregistered)?

  *Error cases to handle:*                                                                                                                                                                                                                      

* 404 — AI cluster garbage collected or user has no privileges → Silent fallback (pre-existing)                                                                                                                                             
* 403 — User not authorized to access AI cluster data → Silent fallback (added in OCMUI-4195)
* 5xx / other — AI service API failure → Silent fallback (added in OCMUI-4195)

  *Proposed direction (pending UX/PM review)*

  Show a non-blocking inline alert (e.g. PatternFly Alert with variant="warning") on the cluster details page when {{useFetchAiCluster}} fails for any reason. The message should communicate that something went wrong and results may be incomplete, without exposing raw error codes.

Example message: "An error occurred retrieving cluster data from Assisted Installer. Showing partial results."
items.toString:
*Background*

[OCMUI-4195|https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/OCMUI-4195] fixed an infinite spinner on the cluster details page for AI (Assisted Installer) clusters when the AI service returns a non-404 error. The fix degrades gracefully by falling back to data from the subscription when the AI cluster API call fails.

  However, this silent degradation means the user has no indication that:

* The AI cluster data could not be retrieved
* The displayed information may be incomplete (partial results)

  *Error cases to handle:*                                                                                                                                                                                                                      

* 404 — AI cluster garbage collected or user has no privileges → Silent fallback (pre-existing)                                                                                                                                             
* 403 — User not authorized to access AI cluster data → Silent fallback (added in OCMUI-4195)
* 5xx / other — AI service API failure → Silent fallback (added in OCMUI-4195)

  *Proposed direction (requires UX/PM review and refinemnt)*

Show a non-blocking inline alert (e.g. PatternFly Alert with variant="warning") on the cluster details page when {{useFetchAiCluster}} fails for any reason. The message should communicate that something went wrong and results may be incomplete, without exposing raw error codes.

Example message: "An error occurred retrieving cluster data from Assisted Installer. Showing partial results."


  *Questions for UX / PM refinement*

* Should all three error types (404, 403, 5xx) surface the same message, or should they be differentiated?
* Is a warning alert the right pattern, or something more subtle (e.g. inline empty-state within the AI-specific section only)?
* Should the alert be dismissible, or persistent for the session?
* Is "showing partial results" the right framing, or should the message be more specific about what data is missing?
* Are there edge cases where silently degrading is the right behavior (e.g. 404 for a cluster that was legitimately deregistered)?

h4. Url: [https://console.dev.redhat.com/openshift/create/osd|https://console.dev.redhat.com/openshift/create/osd|smart-link] 

There are 2 bugs that originate from the same issue:

1. Subscription type 

If the user does not have a quota for creating an OSD cluster, on the billing model page, the annual button should be disabled, and the On-demand subscription type radio button should be selected.

*Reproduction steps*_:_ 

# Use the [myquota|https://gitlab.cee.redhat.com/openshift-group-I/myquota] tool to remove OSD quota (cluster|general-purpose|single|rhinfra|osd|any)
# Open the OSD wizard 
# On the billing model page, no billing model is selected - click next
# Follow the wizard steps and on the overview page observe the billing model

h4. Current Result: 

The annual button is disabled, the on-demand subscription type radio button is not selected, and next succeeds.
On the Review page, the subscription type is shown as "On-Demand: Flexible usage billed through Red Hat Marketplace".

h4. Expected Result:

* On-demand subscription type radio button is selected by default when there is no OSD quota and the annual button is disabled.
* The selected subscription type on the Billing model page matches what is shown on Review.



h4. 
1. Infra type 

If the user does not have quota for Customer cloud subscription and ‘annual’ subscription is chosen, the Red Hat option should be selected by default.

*Reproduction steps*_:_

h3. Summary

The Playwright smoke daily execution is failing or being blocked by Akamai with {{Access Denied}} before requests reach the application. The default parallel workers should be reduced from 4 to 2 to bypass the rate-limit failures.

h3. Context

Log analysis shows this is an infrastructure issue.  
Each Playwright page load triggers about 20-40 requests. With 4 workers navigating at the same time, 80-160 requests hit Akamai from the same IP in seconds. This trips the rate limit.

We already reached out to console dot to analyze the issue: [https://redhat-internal.slack.com/archives/C023VGW21NU/p1782148788775679|https://redhat-internal.slack.com/archives/C023VGW21NU/p1782148788775679|smart-link]

h3. Acceptance criteria

* Reduce the Playwright parallel workers from 4 to 2 temporarily 
* Do this until there is a detailed analysis from the console dot team.
* The change should help bypass the Akamai/CDN rate limit failures.

h3. Other information

Redacting or changing the worker count is not a permanent solution.

*Description:*
The HCC team is changing the cluster logs severity labels and the OCM severity labels need to align with them.
A new notification banner will be added to announce the changes in advance (60 days).
This story also removes severity options ('Error', ‘Fatal’) from the UI that are not supported by the API endpoint - *GET* [+/api/service_logs/v1/cluster_logs/{id}+|https://api.openshift.com/?urls.primaryName=Service%20logs#/default/get_api_service_logs_v1_cluster_logs__id_]+.+

The changes are as follows:

||*Existing labels*||*Proposed Change*||
|Critical|Critical (No change)|
|Major|Important|
|Warning|Moderate|
|Info|Low|
|Debug|Debug|

*Banner:*
- Add to ‘Alerts and recommendations’ section in Cluster Details page
- [Mock|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1iBrC8-8mCfyRyMQ5RU1tQhOWWWcgS9DKLw2Jm0942os/edit?usp=sharing] 

*Acceptance Criteria:*
- Cluster Logs table, filter dropdown, and cluster logs filter chip group use the new labels.
- ‘Error’ and ‘Fatal’ severity options are removed.
- Show information banner to announce the change.
- Relevant tests are updated.

*Implementation:*
Adjust the SEVERITY_TYPES enum in clusterLogConstants.ts file:

{noformat}const SEVERITY_TYPES: string[] = [
  'Debug',
  'Info',
  'Warning',
  'Error',
  'Major',
  'Critical',
  'Fatal',
];{noformat}
